key_insight: A smartphone becomes an interactive, closed-loop tool for collecting targeted corrective demonstrations and instantly improving robot policies, closing the gap between scalable handheld data collection and on-policy correction.
problem_solved: Handheld open-loop demonstrations miss critical failure states and waste labeling effort, while interactive on-robot correction (e.g., DAgger) is costly and hard to scale; this work enables efficient, scalable corrective supervision without needing constant physical interventions.
method: A phone-based interactive interface that presents robot behavior and lets users provide corrective inputs or relabel critical moments.
Active selection of states where the current policy is uncertain or likely to fail, focusing demonstrations on high-value regions of the state distribution.
A low-latency update pipeline that incorporates corrections and fine-tunes or adapts the policy immediately so improvements are realized 'instantly.'
impact: Makes imitation learning more data- and time-efficient by enabling non-expert, in-the-wild users to rapidly fix policy failures; reduces covariate shift and accelerates deployment of robust robot behaviors.
visual_elements: Loop diagram: phone interface -> collect corrective demo -> server/model update -> improved robot behavior
Before/after heatmap or scatter of state coverage showing reduction in failure regions
Line chart of task success rate vs. number of phone corrections (instant improvement after each correction)
Phone UI mockup showing corrective control, uncertainty highlights, and quick-submit workflow
paper_title: RoboPocket: Improve Robot Policies Instantly with Your Phone
paper_authors: Junjie Fang, Wendi Chen, Han Xue, Fangyuan Zhou, Tian Le
